text: Albert Einstein developed the theory of relativity while working at the Swiss Patent Office in Bern. He published four groundbreaking papers in 1905, his annus mirabilis, covering the photoelectric effect, Brownian motion, special relativity, and mass-energy equivalence (E=mc²). Einstein later joined the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton after fleeing Nazi Germany in 1933. He received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1921 for his explanation of the photoelectric effect, not for relativity as commonly assumed.
